correctness.rationale: The two laws share the exact component formula ℓ(1+r_i u_i)[tanh(βh_i+κx_i)−x_i], with u_i=0 for direct response. The multiplier is positive, giving strict inward pointing at ±1. At a coordinate with magnitude M, orient its sign to be positive. The oriented filtered field is increasing in the oriented r_i since 1−M tanh(κM)>0; using |h_i|≤HM gives the envelope ℓ(1+RU)[tanh(cM)−M], with R,U≥0. This proves global attraction and uniqueness for c≤1, including equality by the cubic bound M−tanh M≥b_*M³ on [0,1], and the uniform exponential estimate for c<1. For c>1 the common eigenvalue is positive and the scalar diagonal is inward at 1; symmetry yields both nonzero equilibria. At c=1 put m=(x_++x_-)/2, p=(x_+−x_-)/2. The symmetries make the m equation odd in m and even in p, and the p equation odd in p and even in m. On the common axis the input is m−β(1−τ)ρα³m³/3+O(m⁵). Applying tanh yields cubic −Qm³/3 and the multiplier 1+O(m²) does not change it. The p eigenvalue is −ℓβ(1−τ)(1−η)a<0 under the actual hypotheses. Global entry near zero gives exponential p decay. If m starts nonzero it keeps its sign and (log|m|)′→0, so p²/m²→0. Then (m^−2)′→2ℓQ/3, proving the signed amplitude in physical time. If m starts at zero it stays there and only the exponential mode remains. This derivation also covers α=0 or ρ=0 when a>0; there is no assumed uniform transverse rate as coupling tends to zero. The scripts and numerical notes were inspected, not used as proof of the asymptotic.

value.rationale: For an existing nonlinear model the local threshold need not settle the basin or the marginal rate. The global exact transition and critical law identify when every state reaches neutral consensus, which initial states bypass the slow mode, and how reformulation changes its amplitude independently of mixing contrast. That makes both the parameter threshold and the exact coefficient useful as benchmarks, without generalizing beyond the two-group setting.
